basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Distinguishes instants on a time scale from local civil times, which need a time zone and rules to resolve.
Holiday and working-day calendars are jurisdiction data from authorities, not computed facts.
It differs from scheduling applications, which use these values to plan events.
Every computed result records the reference data releases used.

may: Resolve a local time to an instant using a pinned time zone release.
Compute deadlines and business days for a jurisdiction.
mustNot: Accept or emit a local time without a time zone or binding mode.
Use expired or outdated time zone or holiday data silently.
Choose one observance date where communities legitimately differ.
Assume all days, hours or months have equal length.
requiresHuman: Recording a civil time or holiday authority decision.

considerations: Missed deadlines can cost people rights, money or benefits.
Religious and cultural calendars deserve equal treatment, not one default.

items: Temporal values are recognised by format, offset or zone name, and calendar system.
Confused with a floating local time, a date without zone, a duration and a period.
Off-by-one-hour errors around daylight saving transitions.
Leap second and leap year errors.
